boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission outdoor activities at nearby Swatara State Park, using documented trails, waterways, and historic features.

cards.title: Walk the Swatara Rail Trail
cards.subtitle: Swatara State Park, north of Annville
cards.notes: Bring water, choose a turnaround point together, and use the park map before heading out on the former rail corridor.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission group walk on Swatara State Park’s named rail trail.
cards.evidence_claim: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee; DCNR identifies the Swatara Rail Trail at Swatara State Park.
cards.access_notes: Swatara State Park is open daily, sunrise to sunset; day-use areas close at dusk.

cards.title: Ride the Bear Hole Trail
cards.subtitle: Swatara State Park, north of Annville
cards.notes: Plan a daylight bike ride on the named Bear Hole Trail and check the park map for route conditions before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A bring-your-own-bike outing on a documented Swatara trail.
cards.evidence_claim: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee; DCNR identifies Bear Hole Trail as a bike ride at Swatara State Park.
cards.access_notes: Use a personal bike and visit during the park’s daily sunrise-to-sunset hours.

cards.title: Loop the Northern Multi-use Trail
cards.subtitle: Swatara State Park, north of Annville
cards.notes: Use the official map to locate the Northern Multi-use Loop, then set a relaxed group pace and stay on marked routes.
cards.short_summary: A mapped loop ride for a daytime outdoor hang.
cards.evidence_claim: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee; DCNR lists the Northern Multi-use Loop among Swatara State Park rides.
cards.access_notes: Use a personal bike and visit during the park’s daily sunrise-to-sunset hours.

cards.title: Loop the Southern Multi-use Trail
cards.subtitle: Swatara State Park, north of Annville
cards.notes: Choose the Southern Multi-use Loop from the park guide, ride with a buddy, and leave enough time to return before dusk.
cards.short_summary: A distinct documented loop ride in the state park.
cards.evidence_claim: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee; DCNR lists the Southern Multi-use Loop among Swatara State Park rides.
cards.access_notes: Use a personal bike and visit during the park’s daily sunrise-to-sunset hours.

cards.title: Watch Wildlife Along Swatara Creek
cards.subtitle: Swatara State Park, north of Annville
cards.notes: Pause along the creek corridor to look and listen for wildlife; keep a respectful distance and pack out all trash.
cards.short_summary: A low-key creekside nature watch in a documented wetland landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee; DCNR lists wildlife watching at Swatara State Park.
cards.access_notes: The park is open every day, sunrise to sunset; day-use areas close at dusk.

cards.title: Find the Union Canal Lock Remains
cards.subtitle: Swatara State Park, north of Annville
cards.notes: Use DCNR’s Union Canal map to locate visible lock remains, then photograph from established paths without climbing on ruins.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided look at documented remnants of the Union Canal.
cards.evidence_claim: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee; DCNR documents visible Union Canal lock remains in Swatara State Park.
cards.access_notes: Visit in daylight during the park’s daily sunrise-to-sunset operating window.

cards.title: Spot the Union Canal Towpath Bridge
cards.subtitle: Swatara State Park, north of Annville
cards.notes: Follow the official canal map with friends and view the historic towpath bridge from permitted trail areas only.
cards.short_summary: A history-focused walk to a documented canal-era feature.
cards.evidence_claim: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee; DCNR documents a surviving Union Canal towpath bridge in Swatara State Park.
cards.access_notes: Visit in daylight during the park’s daily sunrise-to-sunset operating window.

cards.title: Walk to Waterville Bridge
cards.subtitle: Swatara State Park, north of Annville
cards.notes: Make the bridge your shared destination, keep to the marked route, and give yourself time to return before day-use closes.
cards.short_summary: A destination walk to Swatara’s relocated historic truss bridge.
cards.evidence_claim: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee; DCNR documents Waterville Bridge as a rebuilt crossing in Swatara State Park.
cards.access_notes: The park is open every day, sunrise to sunset; day-use areas close at dusk.

cards.title: Trace the Canal’s Dam Sites
cards.subtitle: Swatara State Park, north of Annville
cards.notes: Use the Union Canal map to orient your walk and discuss the waterway’s history while staying on public, established routes.
cards.short_summary: A map-led outdoor history activity around documented canal dams.
cards.evidence_claim: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee; DCNR documents three remaining Union Canal dams in Swatara State Park.
cards.access_notes: Visit in daylight during the park’s daily sunrise-to-sunset operating window.

cards.title: Pack a Creekside Picnic Break
cards.subtitle: Swatara State Park, north of Annville
cards.notes: Bring food from home, choose a lawful day-use stop near the creek, and carry every scrap back out with your group.
cards.short_summary: A bring-your-own-food outdoor pause beside Swatara Creek.
cards.evidence_claim: Pennsylvania state parks do not charge an entrance fee; DCNR identifies Swatara Creek as running through Swatara State Park.
cards.access_notes: The park uses carry-in/carryout disposal; visit daily from sunrise to sunset.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named stops along Annville corridors beside Lebanon Valley College, each drawn from the Annville Heritage Trail.

cards.title: The Allen Theatre: Annville’s revival marker
cards.subtitle: East Main Street corridor — 36 E. Main St.
cards.notes: Walk the East Main Street block to see the theatre identified by the heritage trail as part of Annville’s 1995 reopening story.
cards.short_summary: A historic cinema building on the East Main Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The heritage trail identifies The Allen Theatre at 36 E. Main St. and dates its reopening as the Allen to September 21, 1995.
cards.access_notes: Check the theatre’s current program before planning an interior visit.

cards.title: Annville United Methodist Church: blue-marble façade
cards.subtitle: North College Avenue corridor — 1 N. College Ave.
cards.notes: Pause at the College Avenue corner and look for the church’s Pennsylvania blue-marble construction noted on the heritage trail.
cards.short_summary: A 1912 church at the College Avenue and Main Street corner.
cards.evidence_claim: The heritage trail lists Annville United Methodist Church at 1 N. College Ave., dedicated in 1912 and built with King of Prussia marble.
cards.access_notes: Observe the exterior from public areas; verify service or visitor access separately.

cards.title: Kettering Corner: a circa-1780 storefront conversion
cards.subtitle: West Main Street corridor — 104 W. Main St.
cards.notes: Follow West Main Street to this named corner and compare its Georgian details with the trail’s account of its first-floor store use.
cards.short_summary: A named historic corner building on West Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The heritage trail identifies Kettering Corner at 104 W. Main St., describing Georgian decoration and a first floor later converted to a store.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is the appropriate default; individual occupants control any interior access.

cards.title: Batdorf Building: stonework from 1810
cards.subtitle: West Main Street corridor — 103 W. Main St.
cards.notes: On the West Main Street block, look closely at the building’s cut-stone front and the contrasting rubble-stone side walls.
cards.short_summary: A stone commercial-era building with documented construction details.
cards.evidence_claim: The heritage trail places the Batdorf Building at 103 W. Main St., dates it to 1810, and distinguishes its cut-stone front from rubble side walls.
cards.access_notes: View architectural details from public sidewalks; check the current occupant for entry information.

cards.title: Heilman House: Victorian addition on an earlier house
cards.subtitle: West Main Street corridor — 115 W. Main St.
cards.notes: Keep west along Main Street and look for the ornate Victorian addition that the trail says joined an early stone house.
cards.short_summary: A layered historic house with both early-stone and Victorian-era elements.
cards.evidence_claim: The heritage trail identifies Heilman House at 115 W. Main St.; it says the Victorian addition was built in 1901 and the original stone house dates as early as 1810.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing only unless the current property occupant offers access.

cards.title: Oddfellows’ Hall: former jail and auditorium
cards.subtitle: West Main Street corridor — 219 W. Main St.
cards.notes: Continue along West Main Street and use the trail’s history to spot a building once shared by civic, fire, and lodge uses.
cards.short_summary: A former multi-use civic hall on West Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The heritage trail lists Oddfellows’ Hall at 219 W. Main St.; it says the first floor held the town jail and Rescue Fire Company and the second floor was a public auditorium.
cards.access_notes: The trail notes that the building now contains living units; view it from public areas.

cards.title: Washington House: an 18th-century hotel form
cards.subtitle: West Main Street corridor — 245 W. Main St.
cards.notes: At this West Main Street address, look for the original corner doorway, pent eaves, and large stone lintels described by the trail.
cards.short_summary: A historic hotel building with surviving exterior features.
cards.evidence_claim: The heritage trail identifies Washington House at 245 W. Main St. as an attractive hotel built around 1795 and notes its original corner entrance and stone lintels.
cards.access_notes: View exterior features from the public sidewalk; verify any current business access independently.

cards.title: Log House: pre-Revolution saltbox profile
cards.subtitle: West Main Street corridor — 437 W. Main St.
cards.notes: Extend west on Main Street to identify the steep saltbox roof and split-wood red-oak shingles described on the heritage trail.
cards.short_summary: A named pre-Revolution-style house on the West Main Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The heritage trail lists the Log House at 437 W. Main St. as a pre-Revolution New England saltbox-style house with a steep roof and split-wood red-oak shingles.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing only; this is a residential property.

cards.title: Flour Mill: Annville’s long-running milling site
cards.subtitle: West Queen Street corridor — 545 W. Queen St.
cards.notes: Detour one block south of West Main Street to see the four-story frame-and-stone mill complex noted by the heritage trail.
cards.short_summary: A historic mill complex on the West Queen Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The heritage trail identifies the Flour Mill at 545 W. Queen St. and states that a precursor is attested as early as March 10, 1752.
cards.access_notes: View the complex from public areas; confirm any on-site access with its current operator.

cards.title: Jerusalem Cemetery: an early Annville burial ground
cards.subtitle: South White Oak Street corridor — 200 S. White Oak St.
cards.notes: Take South White Oak Street to this named cemetery site and read the trail’s account of Annville pioneers buried there in the 1800s.
cards.short_summary: A documented early burial-ground site on South White Oak Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The heritage trail lists Jerusalem Cemetery at 200 S. White Oak St. and says many Annville pioneers were buried there between 1804 and 1895.
cards.access_notes: Treat the site as a cemetery and follow posted rules and any access restrictions.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Lebanon Valley College traditions and recurring campus celebrations, from a football-win march to seasonal gatherings.

cards.title: Dear Old LVC
cards.subtitle: Lebanon Valley College alma mater
cards.notes: Read the alma mater before a major campus gathering, then listen for its references to “dear old L.V.C.” and its historic authors.
cards.short_summary: LVC’s alma mater was written by Max F. Lehman ’07 and Earle A. Spessard ’11.
cards.evidence_claim: Lebanon Valley College identifies “Dear Old LVC” as its alma mater and credits Max F. Lehman, Class of 1907, and Earle A. Spessard, Class of 1911.
cards.access_notes: Check College event programming for performances or ceremonial use.

cards.title: The Regalia Receiving Line
cards.subtitle: New-student academic-year opening
cards.notes: Incoming students should plan for the formal opening ceremony and its receiving line of faculty, administrators, and trustees in academic regalia.
cards.short_summary: A formal opening-of-year ceremony with a regalia-clad receiving line for new students.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC says Opening Convocation formally opens the academic year and leads all new students through a receiving line of faculty, administration, and trustees in full academic regalia.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation | Lebanon Valley College
cards.access_notes: Listed as required for incoming students in LVC’s new-student orientation schedule.

cards.title: Thanksgiving Dinner
cards.subtitle: Family-style campus meal before break
cards.notes: Watch for the student sign-up and reserve a place at this sit-down meal before leaving campus for the Thanksgiving holiday break.
cards.short_summary: Faculty, staff, administrators, and the president serve this family-style student dinner.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC describes Thanksgiving Dinner as a tradition: a sit-down, family-style meal served by faculty, staff, administrators, and the president, with students signing up before break.
cards.access_notes: Students sign up for the meal; consult current College announcements for availability.

cards.title: March to Kreiderheim
cards.subtitle: Following an LVC football win over Albright
cards.notes: If LVC defeats Albright, join the organized campus march behind the football team, band, and cheerleaders to request extra Thanksgiving break time.
cards.short_summary: A contingent football-win march to the president’s house to request an additional day off.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC states that, after a football win over rival Albright, students march to the president’s house at Kreiderheim to request an extra day off for Thanksgiving break.
cards.access_notes: Occurs only when LVC football defeats Albright; follow College and event-leader directions.

cards.title: Hot Dog Frank Day
cards.subtitle: Annual basketball-season athletics tradition
cards.notes: Check the basketball schedule for this annual game-day observance, including the halftime Athletic Service Award presentation and free hot dogs for fans.
cards.short_summary: A basketball-season observance honoring Annville supporter Frank “Hot Dog” Aftosmes.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC calls Hot Dog Frank Day an annual basketball-season tradition honoring Frank Aftosmes; fans receive free hot dogs and an Athletic Service Award is presented at halftime.
cards.access_notes: Look to the current athletics schedule for the designated game.

cards.title: Christmas at The Valley
cards.subtitle: Annual music and candle-lighting program
cards.notes: Attend the early-December program for LVC choir carols, readings, instrumental music, sing-along hymns, and the candle-lighting service.
cards.short_summary: LVC’s traditional community holiday program combines choirs, readings, and candlelight.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC describes Christmas at The Valley as its traditional gift to the local community, presented the first Sunday in December with readings, carols, instrumental music, sing-along hymns, and candle lighting.
cards.access_notes: LVC lists it for the first Sunday in December; confirm current performance details before attending.

cards.title: ValleyFest
cards.subtitle: LVC’s annual late-April college-and-community festival
cards.notes: Plan an April campus visit for the festival’s arts programming, music, activities, vendors, and community-facing events; details change each year.
cards.short_summary: An annual LVC spring arts and community festival with roots in the 1971 Spring Arts Festival.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC says ValleyFest is an annual tradition that began as the Spring Arts Festival in 1971 and became ValleyFest: A College and Community Festival in fall 2004.
cards.source_title: ValleyFest - Student Life | Lebanon Valley College
cards.access_notes: Usually held at the end of April; consult the current ValleyFest page for programming.

cards.title: Dutchmen Day
cards.subtitle: Annual spring afternoon off from classes
cards.notes: Keep an eye on the spring calendar for an afternoon of games, inflatables, DIY crafts, and other campus programming after classes pause.
cards.short_summary: A yearly spring campus celebration built around an afternoon away from classes.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC describes Dutchmen Day as an annual spring tradition in which students have an afternoon off from classes for games, inflatables, DIY crafts, and more.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled activities vary; follow current Student Engagement announcements.

cards.title: Jingle Jam
cards.subtitle: End-of-fall-classes gathering in the LVC Sports Center
cards.notes: Mark the end of fall classes with the campus’s winter gathering, which features games, crafts, contests, snacks, and changing seasonal activities.
cards.short_summary: An annual LVC winter event that brings students together as fall classes end.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC states that Jingle Jam marks the end of fall classes and is an annual event hosted in the LVC Sports Center with games, crafts, contests, snacks, and more.
cards.access_notes: Hosted in the LVC Sports Center; verify the current date and program with Student Engagement.

cards.title: Winter Formal
cards.subtitle: Student Government’s semi-formal community dinner dance
cards.notes: Watch Student Government announcements for the off-campus semi-formal dinner dance, then follow the event’s registration and transportation guidance.
cards.short_summary: A recurring Student Government-sponsored dinner dance for the College community.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC describes Winter Formal as a Student Government-sponsored semi-formal dinner dance for the College community, held at an off-campus venue with food and music.
cards.access_notes: Off-campus location and participation details are announced for each event.
